questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Crop Production: Introduction and Modern Agriculture
questions.sub_topic: Group to which sugar beet belongs
questions.question: Sugarcane and sugar beet are both classified as:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) sugar crops
Why: Both are grown for the sucrose stored in their stems (sugarcane) or roots (sugar beet).
Why not the others: They are not grown for (A) fibre, (B) forage or (C) oil.
Key point: Sugar crops: sugarcane and sugar beet.

questions.topic: Unit 2 (Livestock Production): Livestock: Care, Management and Diseases
questions.sub_topic: Care of the pregnant cow and newborn calf — which hold
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(A) A pregnant cow should be dried off about two months before calving.
(B) She should be housed separately in a clean calving pen as calving nears.
(C) She should get a little extra concentrate in the last months of pregnancy.
(D) The navel of the newborn calf should be dipped in tincture of iodine.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A), (B), (C) and (D)
Why: All four are standard practices. A dry period rests the udder, a calving pen keeps the cow safe and clean, extra feed supports the growing foetus, and iodine on the navel prevents infection.
Why not the others: Options (A), (B) and (D) each leave out at least one correct practice.
Key point: Dry off, feed up, keep clean, dip the navel.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Microbiology
questions.sub_topic: Microbial groups and examples
questions.question:
Match List-I (Group) with List-II (Example).

List-I
(A) Fungus
(B) Actinomycete
(C) Protozoan
(D) Virus

List-II
(I) *Amoeba*
(II) *Aspergillus*
(III) Tobacco mosaic virus
(IV) *Streptomyces*
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A)-(II), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(III)
Why: *Aspergillus* is a fungus (II). *Streptomyces* is an actinomycete (IV). *Amoeba* is a protozoan (I). TMV is a virus (III).
Why not the others: Option (A) swaps the fungus and actinomycete. Option (C) swaps the protozoan and virus. Option (D) swaps the fungus and protozoan.
Key point: Know one example of each microbial group.

questions.topic: Unit 4 (Horticulture): Horticulture: Importance, Orchards, Gardens and Propagation
questions.sub_topic: Plants that need support
questions.question: Plants such as bougainvillea and money plant, which need support to grow upward, are called:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) climbers
Why: Climbers have weak stems and climb on supports using tendrils, twining stems or hooks.
Why not the others:
(A) Shrubs stand on their own.
(B) Annuals are defined by life span.
(D) Trees have a strong trunk.
Key point: Climbers need support.

questions.topic: Unit 2 (Livestock Production): Artificial Insemination and Livestock Products
questions.sub_topic: Best time to inseminate a cow seen in heat in the morning
questions.question: By the a.m.–p.m. rule, a cow first seen in heat in the morning should be inseminated:
options: A) at once, the same morning
B) only after the heat has ended two days later
C) in the evening of the same day
D) during her next heat three weeks later
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) in the evening of the same day
Why: Ovulation occurs some hours after heat ends. Insemination about 12 hours after heat is first seen gives the best chance of conception, so a morning heat is served the same evening.
Why not the others:
(A) This is too early.
(B) This is too late.
(D) Waiting three weeks wastes a heat cycle.
Key point: Seen in the morning, serve in the evening; seen in the evening, serve the next morning.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Irrigation and Drainage
questions.sub_topic: Types of drainage and their features
questions.question:
Match List-I (Drainage type) with List-II (Feature).

List-I
(A) Surface drains
(B) Tile drains
(C) Mole drains
(D) Vertical drainage

List-II
(I) Unlined channels made in clay subsoil by a bullet-shaped plough
(II) Pumping from wells to lower the water table
(III) Open ditches that remove excess water from the land surface
(IV) Perforated pipes buried below the ground
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)
Why: Surface drains are open ditches (III). Tile drains are buried perforated pipes (IV). Mole drains are unlined channels made by a mole plough (I). Vertical drainage pumps from wells to lower the water table (II).
Why not the others: Option (B) swaps surface and tile drains. Option (C) swaps tile and mole drains. Option (D) swaps mole and vertical drainage.
Key point: Surface drainage removes ponded water; subsurface drainage lowers the water table.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Microbiology
questions.sub_topic: Why earthworms help farmers
questions.question: Why are earthworms called the farmer's friend?
options: A) Because they feed on the roots of weeds growing in the field
B) Because they fix nitrogen from the air just as Rhizobium does
C) Because they kill all the harmful fungi present in the soil
D) Because their burrows aerate the soil and their casts enrich it
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Because their burrows aerate the soil and their casts enrich it
Why: Earthworm burrows improve aeration and drainage, and their casts are rich in available nutrients and humus.
Why not the others:
(A) They feed on decaying organic matter, not on living weed roots.
(B) They do not fix nitrogen.
(C) They do not kill all harmful fungi.
Key point: Earthworms till and enrich the soil.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Genetics and Plant Breeding
questions.sub_topic: Chemical used to induce polyploidy
questions.question: Which chemical is widely used to double the chromosome number and induce polyploidy in plants?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Colchicine
Why: Colchicine stops spindle fibres from forming, so the chromosomes divide but the cell does not, which doubles the chromosome number.
Why not the others:
(A) Gibberellic acid promotes stem growth and germination.
(B) Ethylene promotes ripening.
(D) IBA promotes rooting of cuttings.
Key point: Colchicine blocks the spindle and doubles chromosomes.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Genetics and Plant Breeding
questions.sub_topic: Ability of a plant cell to form a whole plant
questions.question: The ability of a single plant cell to grow into a complete plant, which is the basis of tissue culture, is called ________.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) totipotency
Why: Totipotency is the capacity of a cell to divide and differentiate into a whole plant.
Why not the others:
(B) Heterosis is hybrid vigour.
(C) Apomixis is seed formation without fertilisation.
(D) Polyembryony is the presence of more than one embryo in a seed.
Key point: Tissue culture rests on totipotency.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Weed Control
questions.sub_topic: How nut grass spreads
questions.question: *Cyperus rotundus* (nut grass) is hard to control mainly because it spreads by:
options: C) runners on the soil surface
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) underground tubers
Why: Nut grass forms chains of underground tubers. Each tuber can sprout again after the top growth is removed.
Why not the others:
(A) Seed is not its main means of spread.
(B) It is a flowering plant, not a spore-bearer.
(C) Surface runners are typical of Bermuda grass.
Key point: Nut grass survives on its tubers.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Agrometeorology
questions.sub_topic: Types of weather forecast — which hold
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about weather forecasts:
(A) Short-range forecasts cover a period of up to about 3 days.
(B) Medium-range forecasts cover about 3 to 10 days.
(C) Long-range (extended) forecasts are for periods beyond 10 days, up to a season.
(D) Nowcasts are forecasts for the next six months.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A), (B) and (C) only
Why: (A), (B) and (C) describe the usual ranges. (D) is false: a nowcast covers only the next few hours.
Why not the others: Options (A) and (C) include the false statement (D). Option (B) leaves out the true statement (A).
Key point: Nowcast — hours; short — up to 3 days; medium — 3–10 days; long — beyond 10 days.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Microbiology
questions.sub_topic: What a virus particle is made of
questions.question: A virus particle consists of:
options: A) nucleic acid enclosed in a protein coat
B) a nucleus, cytoplasm and a cell wall
C) chlorophyll in a lipid membrane
D) many cells joined into a filament
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) nucleic acid enclosed in a protein coat
Why: A virus has a core of DNA or RNA inside a protein coat (capsid) and no cellular structure of its own.
Why not the others:
(B) Viruses have no nucleus, cytoplasm or wall.
(C) Viruses have no chlorophyll.
(D) Viruses are not cellular.
Key point: Virus = nucleic acid + protein coat.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Biochemistry
questions.sub_topic: Lipids — which statements are wrong
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(A) Fats are esters of glycerol and fatty acids.
(B) Unsaturated fatty acids have one or more double bonds in their carbon chain.
(C) Lipids dissolve readily in water.
(D) Saturated fats such as ghee are usually liquid at room temperature.
Which of the statements given above are NOT correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (C) and (D) only
Why: (A) and (B) are true. (C) is false: lipids are insoluble in water and dissolve in organic solvents. (D) is false: saturated fats such as ghee are solid or semi-solid at room temperature; unsaturated oils are liquid.
Why not the others: Options (A) and (B) call true statements wrong. Option (D) misses statement (C).
Key point: Saturated — solid; unsaturated — liquid; all lipids shun water.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Seed Science
questions.sub_topic: Term for wind pollination
questions.question: Transfer of pollen by wind, as in maize, is called ________.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) anemophily
Why: Anemophily is wind pollination. Wind-pollinated flowers produce light, abundant pollen and feathery stigmas.
Why not the others:
(A) Entomophily is pollination by insects.
(C) Hydrophily is pollination by water.
(D) Ornithophily is pollination by birds.
Key point: Anemo- = wind; entomo- = insect.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Genetics and Plant Breeding
questions.sub_topic: Plant breeding terms and meanings
questions.question:
Match List-I (Term) with List-II (Meaning).

List-I
(A) Heterosis
(B) Emasculation
(C) Polyploidy
(D) Mutation

List-II
(I) A sudden heritable change in a gene or chromosome
(II) The presence of more than two sets of chromosomes
(III) Removal of anthers before the pollen is shed
(IV) The superiority of an F₁ hybrid over its parents
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: Heterosis is hybrid vigour (IV). Emasculation is removing anthers to prevent selfing (III). Polyploidy means more than two chromosome sets (II). Mutation is a sudden heritable change (I).
Why not the others: Option (A) swaps heterosis and emasculation. Option (B) swaps emasculation and polyploidy. Option (C) swaps polyploidy and mutation.
Key point: Heterosis is what hybrid seed sells.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Crop Production: Introduction and Modern Agriculture
questions.sub_topic: Foodgrain production and commercialisation — which hold
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(A) India's foodgrain production in 1950–51 was about 51 million tonnes.
(B) In recent years it has crossed 300 million tonnes.
(C) Commercialisation of agriculture means growing crops only for the farm family's own use.
(D) The Green Revolution in India began in the 1990s.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A) and (B) only
Why: (A) and (B) are true: production rose from about 51 million tonnes in 1950–51 to over 300 million tonnes in the 2020s. (C) is false: commercialisation means producing for the market. (D) is false: the Green Revolution began in the mid-1960s.
Why not the others: Options (B), (C) and (D) all include at least one false statement.
Key point: About 51 Mt in 1950–51; over 300 Mt now.

questions.topic: Unit 4 (Horticulture): Horticulture: Importance, Orchards, Gardens and Propagation
questions.sub_topic: Another name for air layering
questions.question: Air layering, used to propagate guava and litchi, is also known as:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) gootee
Why: Air layering, also called gootee or marcotting, roots a stem while it is still on the plant, by wrapping a ringed portion in moist moss.
Why not the others:
(A) Stooling is mound layering at the base.
(C) Trench layering buries a whole shoot in a trench.
(D) Shield budding is T-budding.
Key point: Air layering = gootee = marcotting.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Weed Control
questions.sub_topic: An aquatic weed
questions.question: Which of the following is an aquatic weed?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) *Eichhornia crassipes* (water hyacinth)
Why: Water hyacinth floats on water and chokes ponds, canals and lakes.
Why not the others: (B) Parthenium, (C) Bermuda grass and (D) bathua are land weeds.
Key point: Water hyacinth is the worst aquatic weed in India.

questions.topic: Unit 2 (Livestock Production): Livestock: Scope, Importance and Breeds
questions.sub_topic: India's rank in world milk production
questions.question: India's rank among the milk-producing countries of the world is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) first
Why: India has been the world's largest milk producer since the late 1990s.
Why not the others: India ranks first, not (B) second, (C) fifth or (D) tenth.
Key point: India is the world's top milk producer.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Genetics and Plant Breeding
questions.sub_topic: Base not found in DNA
questions.question: Which of the following nitrogenous bases is NOT found in DNA?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Uracil
Why: DNA contains adenine, guanine, cytosine and thymine. Uracil replaces thymine in RNA.
Why not the others: (A) thymine, (C) cytosine and (D) guanine are all DNA bases.
Key point: T in DNA, U in RNA.

questions.topic: Unit 2 (Livestock Production): Livestock: Care, Management and Diseases
questions.sub_topic: How coccidiosis spreads in chicks
questions.question: Coccidiosis in young chicks spreads mainly through:
options: A) damp litter contaminated with oocysts in droppings
B) the bite of mosquitoes at night
C) contact with infected cattle in the same yard
D) eggs that are laid by infected hens
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) damp litter contaminated with oocysts in droppings
Why: The oocysts of *Eimeria* pass out in droppings and sporulate in warm, damp litter. Chicks pick them up while pecking. Dry litter and coccidiostats prevent outbreaks.
Why not the others:
(B) Mosquitoes spread fowl pox, not coccidiosis.
(C) Cattle coccidia are different species.
(D) It is not transmitted through eggs.
Key point: Keep the litter dry to prevent coccidiosis.

questions.topic: Unit 4 (Horticulture): Cultivation of Fruits, Vegetables and Flowers
questions.sub_topic: Vegetables and their botanical families
questions.question:
Match List-I (Vegetable) with List-II (Family).

List-I
(A) Carrot
(B) Onion
(C) Spinach
(D) Brinjal

List-II
(I) Apiaceae (Umbelliferae)
(II) Solanaceae
(III) Amaryllidaceae (Alliaceae)
(IV) Chenopodiaceae (now Amaranthaceae)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A)-(I), (B)-(III), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II)
Why: Carrot belongs to Apiaceae (I). Onion belongs to the onion family, Amaryllidaceae (Alliaceae) (III). Spinach belongs to Chenopodiaceae, now placed in Amaranthaceae (IV). Brinjal belongs to Solanaceae (II).
Why not the others: Option (B) swaps carrot and onion. Option (C) swaps onion and spinach. Option (D) swaps spinach and brinjal.
Key point: Brinjal, tomato and potato share Solanaceae.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Field Crops: Cultivation, Protection and Post-harvest
questions.sub_topic: Crops and their botanical names
questions.question:
Match List-I (Crop) with List-II (Botanical name).

List-I
(A) Pigeon pea
(B) Gram
(C) Pearl millet
(D) Sorghum

List-II
(I) *Sorghum bicolor*
(II) *Cajanus cajan*
(III) *Pennisetum glaucum*
(IV) *Cicer arietinum*
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A)-(II), (B)-(IV), (C)-(III), (D)-(I)
Why: Pigeon pea is *Cajanus cajan* (II). Gram is *Cicer arietinum* (IV). Pearl millet is *Pennisetum glaucum* (III). Sorghum is *Sorghum bicolor* (I).
Why not the others: Option (A) swaps pigeon pea and gram. Option (C) swaps gram and pearl millet. Option (D) swaps pearl millet and sorghum.
Key point: Learn the botanical names of the major field crops.

questions.topic: Unit 2 (Livestock Production): Livestock: Care, Management and Diseases
questions.sub_topic: Cattle disease that is not viral
questions.question: Which of the following diseases is NOT caused by a virus?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Black quarter
Why: Black quarter is a bacterial disease caused by *Clostridium chauvoei*.
Why not the others: (A) rinderpest, (B) FMD and (C) fowl pox are all viral diseases.
Key point: BQ and HS are bacterial; rinderpest, FMD and fowl pox are viral.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Soil, Soil Fertility, Fertilizers and Manures
questions.sub_topic: A complex fertilizer
questions.question: Which of the following is a complex fertilizer?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) NPK 10:26:26
Why: A complex fertilizer contains two or more major nutrients combined chemically in each granule; NPK 10:26:26 supplies N, P and K.
Why not the others: (B) urea (N), (C) MOP (K) and (D) SSP (P) are straight fertilizers, each giving one major nutrient.
Key point: Straight — one nutrient; complex — two or more in one granule.

questions.topic: Unit 2 (Livestock Production): Livestock: Scope, Importance and Breeds
questions.sub_topic: Type of breed Rhode Island Red is
questions.question: Rhode Island Red is:
options: A) an indigenous broiler breed of Andhra Pradesh
B) an indigenous game bird of Punjab
C) a breed of duck reared for eggs
D) an exotic dual-purpose breed of fowl
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) an exotic dual-purpose breed of fowl
Why: Rhode Island Red, from the USA, is an exotic breed kept for both eggs and meat.
Why not the others:
(A) and (B) It is not an Indian breed.
(C) It is a fowl, not a duck.
Key point: Rhode Island Red is an exotic dual-purpose fowl.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Biochemistry
questions.sub_topic: A fat-soluble vitamin
questions.question: Which of the following vitamins is NOT water-soluble?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Vitamin K
Why: Vitamin K is fat-soluble, like vitamins A, D and E.
Why not the others: (A) B₁, (B) C and (D) B₁₂ are water-soluble vitamins.
Key point: Fat-soluble vitamins: A, D, E, K.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Biochemistry
questions.sub_topic: What a buffer solution does
questions.question: A buffer solution is one that:
options: A) always has a pH of exactly 7, whatever is added to it
B) contains only a strong acid dissolved in plain water
C) changes its pH sharply when even a little acid is added
D) resists a change in pH when a little acid or alkali is added
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) resists a change in pH when a little acid or alkali is added
Why: A buffer, usually a weak acid with its salt, absorbs added H⁺ or OH⁻ ions and keeps the pH nearly constant.
Why not the others:
(A) Buffers can hold any pH, not only 7.
(B) A strong acid alone is not a buffer.
(C) This is the opposite of what a buffer does.
Key point: Buffers keep pH steady; soil and blood are buffered.

questions.topic: Unit 4 (Horticulture): Cultivation of Fruits, Vegetables and Flowers
questions.sub_topic: Crop affected by Panama wilt
questions.question: 'Panama wilt', caused by *Fusarium oxysporum* f. sp. *cubense*, is a serious disease of:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) banana
Why: Panama wilt is a soil-borne fungal disease of banana. It yellows and wilts the leaves and discolours the vascular tissue of the pseudostem.
Why not the others: (A) mango, (B) guava and (C) papaya are not hosts of this forma specialis.
Key point: Panama wilt — banana; use resistant varieties and clean suckers.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Agrometeorology
questions.sub_topic: Why cloudy nights stay warmer
questions.question: Why is a cloudy night usually warmer than a clear night, with less risk of frost on crops?
options: A) Because clouds give off heat by condensing water all night
B) Because clouds absorb and send back the heat radiated by the ground
C) Because clouds bring warm winds from the sea every night
D) Because clouds reflect moonlight, which warms the soil
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Because clouds absorb and send back the heat radiated by the ground
Why: At night the ground loses heat as long-wave radiation. Clouds absorb much of it and radiate part of it back, so the ground cools less.
Why not the others:
(A) Condensation is not a steady night-long heat source of this kind.
(C) Clouds do not bring sea winds.
(D) Moonlight carries almost no heat.
Key point: Clear, calm nights bring frost; clouds act like a blanket.

questions.topic: Unit 2 (Livestock Production): Livestock: Scope, Importance and Breeds
questions.sub_topic: Cattle breeds and home states
questions.question:
Match List-I (Breed) with List-II (Home state).

List-I
(A) Gir
(B) Ongole
(C) Kangayam
(D) Rathi

List-II
(I) Rajasthan
(II) Tamil Nadu
(III) Gujarat
(IV) Andhra Pradesh
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: Gir comes from Gujarat (III). Ongole comes from Andhra Pradesh (IV). Kangayam comes from Tamil Nadu (II). Rathi comes from Rajasthan (I).
Why not the others: Option (A) swaps Gir and Ongole. Option (B) swaps Ongole and Kangayam. Option (D) swaps Kangayam and Rathi.
Key point: Breed names often point to their home tract.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Field Crops: Cultivation, Protection and Post-harvest
questions.sub_topic: Order of post-harvest steps for wheat
questions.question:
Arrange the following post-harvest steps for wheat in the correct order.
(A) Storage in bins
(B) Harvesting
(C) Cleaning and drying of grain
(D) Threshing
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (B), (D), (C), (A)
Why: The crop is harvested (B), threshed to separate grain (D), cleaned and dried to safe moisture (C), and then stored (A).
Why not the others: Option (A) cleans before threshing. Option (C) threshes before harvesting. Option (D) stores before drying.
Key point: Harvest → thresh → clean and dry → store.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Soil, Soil Fertility, Fertilizers and Manures
questions.sub_topic: Order of steps in green manuring
questions.question:
Arrange the steps of green manuring with dhaincha in the correct order.
(A) Plough the crop into the soil at flowering
(B) Sow or transplant the main crop
(C) Allow the buried crop to decompose for one to two weeks
(D) Sow dhaincha in the field
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (D), (A), (C), (B)
Why: Dhaincha is sown first (D). It is ploughed in at flowering, when its biomass and nitrogen are highest (A). It is left to decompose (C). Then the main crop is planted (B).
Why not the others: Option (A) decomposes before ploughing. Option (B) ploughs before sowing. Option (C) plants the main crop before decomposition.
Key point: Grow → bury at flowering → decompose → plant.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Genetics and Plant Breeding
questions.sub_topic: Order of substages of prophase I
questions.question:
Arrange the following substages of prophase I of meiosis in the correct order.
(A) Pachytene
(B) Leptotene
(C) Diplotene
(D) Zygotene
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (B), (D), (A), (C)
Why: In leptotene (B) chromosomes become visible as threads. In zygotene (D) homologues pair. In pachytene (A) crossing over takes place. In diplotene (C) the homologues begin to separate, showing chiasmata.
Why not the others: Option (B) starts with zygotene. Option (C) puts pachytene before zygotene. Option (D) puts diplotene before pachytene.
Key point: Leptotene → zygotene → pachytene → diplotene → diakinesis.

questions.topic: Unit 2 (Livestock Production): Livestock: Care, Management and Diseases
questions.sub_topic: Why layers need extra calcium
questions.question: Why are laying hens given extra calcium, for example as shell grit or limestone?
options: A) Because calcium makes the egg yolk a deep yellow colour
B) Because each eggshell is made mostly of calcium carbonate
C) Because calcium protects the flock from Ranikhet disease
D) Because calcium speeds up the growth of the bird's feathers
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Because each eggshell is made mostly of calcium carbonate
Why: An eggshell is mostly calcium carbonate. A layer needs a lot of extra calcium, or she lays thin-shelled eggs and draws on her own bones.
Why not the others:
(A) Yolk colour comes from pigments such as xanthophylls.
(C) Ranikhet is prevented by vaccination.
(D) Feathers are protein.
Key point: No calcium, no strong shells.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Agrometeorology
questions.sub_topic: Unit in which rainfall is reported
questions.question: Rainfall is usually measured and reported in:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) millimetres
Why: Rainfall is the depth of water that would collect on flat ground, so it is reported in millimetres.
Why not the others:
(B) Kilograms measure mass.
(C) Litres per second measure flow.
(D) Hectopascals measure air pressure.
Key point: Rainfall is a depth, measured in mm.

questions.topic: Unit 2 (Livestock Production): Fisheries
questions.sub_topic: Term for rearing fish under controlled conditions
questions.question: The rearing of fish and other aquatic organisms in ponds or tanks under controlled conditions is called:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) aquaculture
Why: Aquaculture is the farming of aquatic organisms under controlled or semi-controlled conditions.
Why not the others:
(A) A capture fishery takes wild fish from natural waters.
(C) Sericulture is silkworm rearing.
(D) Apiculture is beekeeping.
Key point: Aquaculture farms fish; capture fishery catches them.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Field Crops: Cultivation, Protection and Post-harvest
questions.sub_topic: Pearl millet disease that forms toxic sclerotia
questions.question: Which disease of pearl millet replaces grains with hard sclerotia that are poisonous to people and animals?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Ergot
Why: In ergot (*Claviceps*), a sticky honeydew oozes from infected florets and is later replaced by hard, toxic sclerotia.
Why not the others:
(A) Downy mildew (green ear) turns the ear leafy.
(B) Smut turns grains into sacs of black spores.
(D) Rust forms pustules on leaves.
Key point: Ergot sclerotia are poisonous; clean seed by brine flotation.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Irrigation and Drainage
questions.sub_topic: Meaning of a watershed
questions.question: A watershed is best defined as:
options: A) a large tank built to store canal water
B) the line along which a river meets the sea
C) an area of land that drains to a common outlet
D) a wall built across a gully to stop erosion
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) an area of land that drains to a common outlet
Why: A watershed is the land area whose runoff drains to one stream, river or outlet. It is the natural unit for soil and water conservation.
Why not the others:
(A) A tank is a storage structure.
(B) This describes a coastline or estuary.
(D) A check dam is one structure within a watershed.
Key point: Manage land and water by watershed, ridge to valley.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Crop Production: Introduction and Modern Agriculture
questions.sub_topic: Meaning of sustainable crop production
questions.question: Sustainable crop production means:
options: A) using the highest possible doses of fertilizer every season
B) growing one crop continuously on the same land
C) meeting today's needs without harming the resources needed in future
D) farming only by hand without any machines
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) meeting today's needs without harming the resources needed in future
Why: Sustainable agriculture keeps production up while protecting soil, water and biodiversity for future generations.
Why not the others:
(A) Heavy fertilizer use harms soil and water.
(B) Monoculture depletes soil and builds up pests.
(D) Sustainability is not defined by giving up machines.
Key point: Sustainable = productive now, productive later.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Soil, Soil Fertility, Fertilizers and Manures
questions.sub_topic: Manures and INM — which statement is wrong
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(A) Biofertilizers contain synthetic NPK salts in a carrier.
(B) Farmyard manure is a bulky organic manure.
(C) Green manuring with dhaincha adds organic matter and nitrogen to the soil.
(D) Integrated nutrient management combines fertilizers, manures and biofertilizers.
Which of the statements given above is NOT correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A) only
Why: (A) is false: biofertilizers contain living microbes, such as *Rhizobium* or *Azotobacter*, in a carrier, not synthetic salts. (B), (C) and (D) are true.
Why not the others: Statements (B), (C) and (D) are all correct.
Key point: Biofertilizers are living cultures, not chemicals.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Seed Science
questions.sub_topic: Order of events in seed germination
questions.question:
Arrange the events of seed germination in the correct order.
(A) Enzymes are activated and food reserves are mobilised
(B) The plumule emerges above the soil
(C) The seed imbibes water and swells
(D) The radicle emerges from the seed
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (C), (A), (D), (B)
Why: The seed first absorbs water (C). This activates enzymes that break down stored food (A). The radicle emerges first (D), and the plumule follows (B).
Why not the others: Option (A) puts the radicle before enzyme activity. Option (B) starts with enzymes before water uptake. Option (D) puts the plumule before the radicle.
Key point: Imbibition → enzyme activity → radicle → plumule.

questions.topic: Unit 2 (Livestock Production): Artificial Insemination and Livestock Products
questions.sub_topic: Artificial insemination — which statement is wrong
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about artificial insemination:
(A) Semen from one superior bull can be used to breed thousands of cows.
(B) It helps to prevent the spread of some reproductive diseases.
(C) Frozen semen can be used even after the bull has died.
(D) It removes the need to detect heat in cows.
Which of the statements given above is NOT correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (D) only
Why: (D) is false: insemination must be timed to the heat period, so accurate heat detection is essential. (A), (B) and (C) are real advantages of AI.
Why not the others: Statements (A), (B) and (C) are all correct.
Key point: AI spreads good genes widely but still depends on spotting heat.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Irrigation and Drainage
questions.sub_topic: Water needed to irrigate one hectare to 5 cm
questions.question: How much water is needed to irrigate one hectare of land to a depth of 5 cm?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) 500 m³
Why: Step 1: 1 hectare = 10,000 m².
Step 2: depth = 5 cm = 0.05 m.
Step 3: volume = 10,000 × 0.05 = 500 m³.
Why not the others:
(A) 50 m³ is ten times too small.
(C) 5,000 m³ is a 50 cm depth.
(D) 50,000 m³ is a 5 m depth.
Key point: Volume = area × depth; keep the units in metres.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Soil, Soil Fertility, Fertilizers and Manures
questions.sub_topic: Nutrient at the centre of chlorophyll
questions.question: Which nutrient lies at the centre of the chlorophyll molecule?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Magnesium
Why: Each chlorophyll molecule has a magnesium atom at its centre; magnesium deficiency causes interveinal chlorosis of older leaves.
Why not the others:
(A) Iron is needed to make chlorophyll but is not part of it.
(C) Calcium builds cell walls.
(D) Manganese works in photosynthesis enzymes, not at the centre of chlorophyll.
Key point: Mg is at the heart of chlorophyll.

questions.topic: Unit 4 (Horticulture): Fruit and Vegetable Preservation
questions.sub_topic: Three essentials for setting a jelly
questions.question:
Read the following passage and answer the question that follows.

Jam and jelly are among the oldest ways of keeping fruit for the months when it is out of season. Both depend on three things being present in the right balance: pectin, acid and sugar. Pectin is a natural substance found in the cell walls of fruit. Guava, apple and the peel of citrus fruits are rich in it, while fruits such as strawberry and cherry contain little. Acid helps the pectin to form a gel; most jellies set best when the fruit extract is quite acidic, at a pH of roughly 3.0 to 3.5. Sugar draws water away from the pectin so that its chains can join, and at high concentration it also stops microbes from growing. Jam is made by boiling the fruit pulp with sugar until the product is thick. Jelly is made only from the strained, clear juice, so a good jelly is transparent and holds its shape when turned out of the mould. Marmalade is a jelly in which thin shreds of citrus peel are suspended. The cook must judge the end point carefully. One way is the sheet test: when a little of the boiling mass is lifted on a ladle and allowed to fall, it should drop off as a sheet, not as a thin stream. Another way uses a thermometer: the mass is ready when it boils about 5 to 6 °C above the boiling point of water, which is 105 to 106 °C at sea level. The hot product is filled into clean, sterilised jars and sealed at once.

Question: According to the passage, which three things must be present in the right balance for jam and jelly to set?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Pectin, acid and sugar
Why: The passage says that both jam and jelly depend on pectin, acid and sugar being present in the right balance.
Why not the others:
(A) Starch and salt play no setting role.
(B) Protein is not mentioned.
(D) Salt and vinegar are used in pickles, not jelly.
Key point: Pectin + acid + sugar = set.

Question: Which of the following does the passage name as rich in pectin?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Guava
Why: The passage lists guava, apple and citrus peel as rich in pectin.
Why not the others:
(B) and (C) Strawberry and cherry are named as low in pectin.
(D) Grape is not mentioned.
Key point: Guava and citrus peel are good sources of pectin.

questions.topic: Unit 4 (Horticulture): Fruit and Vegetable Preservation
questions.sub_topic: How marmalade differs from jelly

Question: According to the passage, marmalade differs from an ordinary jelly because it:
options: A) is made from the whole fruit pulp, not juice
B) contains no added sugar at all
C) is set with gelatin instead of pectin
D) has thin shreds of citrus peel suspended in it
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) has thin shreds of citrus peel suspended in it
Why: The passage defines marmalade as a jelly in which thin shreds of citrus peel are suspended.
Why not the others:
(A) Whole pulp describes jam.
(B) Marmalade is a sugar product.
(C) Gelatin is not mentioned; pectin is the setting agent.
Key point: Marmalade = jelly + citrus peel shreds.

questions.topic: Unit 4 (Horticulture): Fruit and Vegetable Preservation
questions.sub_topic: Likely reason a jelly fails to set
questions.question:
Read the following passage and answer the question that follows.

Question: A batch of jelly made with the right amount of sugar fails to set. Based on the passage, the most likely cause is that the extract:
options: A) was too clear because it had been strained
B) had too little pectin or was not acidic enough
C) was filled into the jars while still hot
D) was boiled to about 105 °C at sea level
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) had too little pectin or was not acidic enough
Why: The passage says setting needs pectin, acid and sugar in balance. If sugar was correct, the shortfall must lie in pectin or acid.
Why not the others:
(A) Straining is what the passage says jelly needs.
(C) Hot filling is the correct method.
(D) 105 °C at sea level is the correct end point.
Key point: When sugar is right and the jelly is runny, check pectin and acid.

questions.topic: Unit 4 (Horticulture): Fruit and Vegetable Preservation
questions.sub_topic: End point at a hill station
questions.question:
Read the following passage and answer the question that follows.

Jam and jelly are among the oldest ways of keeping fruit for the months when it is out of season. Both depend on three things being present in the right balance: pectin, acid and sugar. Pectin is a natural substance found in the cell walls of fruit. Guava, apple and the peel of citrus fruits are rich in it, while fruits such as strawberry and cherry contain little. Acid helps the pectin to form a gel; most jellies set best when the fruit extract is quite acidic, at a pH of roughly 3.0 to 3.5. Jelly is made only from the strained, clear juice, so a good jelly is transparent and holds its shape when turned out of the mould. Marmalade is a jelly in which thin shreds of citrus peel are suspended. The cook must judge the end point carefully. The hot product is filled into clean, sterilised jars and sealed at once.

Question: In a hill town, water boils at 96 °C. Using the thermometer rule in the passage, at about what temperature has jam reached its end point there?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 101–102 °C
Why: Step 1: the passage says the end point is 5 to 6 °C above the boiling point of water.
Step 2: water boils at 96 °C in the town.
Step 3: 96 + 5 = 101 °C and 96 + 6 = 102 °C.
Why not the others:
(A) and (B) are too close to the boiling point of water; the jam would be thin.
(D) 105–106 °C is the sea-level figure; the rule is relative to local boiling point.
Key point: End point = boiling point of water + 5–6 °C.
